question_text: If (√3 + i)¹⁰⁰ = 2⁹⁹(a + ib), show that a² + b² = 4.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show a² + b² = 4 without expanding the power — what you take on both sides and what cancels.
insider_note: Do not expand the power and do not use De Moivre — take the modulus of both sides: |√3 + i| = 2 gives 2¹⁰⁰ on the left, and the positive real number 2⁹⁹ comes out of the modulus unchanged. The finish is 2¹⁰⁰/2⁹⁹ = 2, then square.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take the modulus
steps.margin_note: First mark. |√3 + i| = √(3 + 1) = 2, so the left side has modulus 2¹⁰⁰. On the right, 2⁹⁹ is a positive real number and comes out of the modulus unchanged.
steps.memory_tip: |zⁿ| = |z|ⁿ. Since |√3 + i| = 2, the left side is 2¹⁰⁰ — no expansion and no De Moivre.

recall.must_convey: That taking the modulus of both sides gives 2¹⁰⁰ = 2⁹⁹ √(a² + b²), because |√3 + i| = 2.
accept: take modulus both sides, mod of root three plus i is two so the left is two to the hundred and the right is two to the ninety nine times root a squared plus b squared

steps.why: |zⁿ| = |z|ⁿ, so the modulus of a huge power is just a power of a small modulus. The question cannot be done by expanding; the modulus is the only sensible tool, and it removes the whole (√3 + i)¹⁰⁰ in one line.
common_mistakes: Trying to expand (√3 + i)¹⁰⁰ or to use De Moivre when only a² + b² is asked.

steps.label: Cancel and square
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide by 2⁹⁹: 2¹⁰⁰/2⁹⁹ = 2. Then square.
steps.memory_tip: 2¹⁰⁰/2⁹⁹ = 2¹ = 2. Then square both sides: a² + b² = 4.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by 2⁹⁹ leaves √(a² + b²) = 2, and squaring gives a² + b² = 4.

steps.why: 2¹⁰⁰ ÷ 2⁹⁹ = 2¹ — subtract the exponents. The remaining equation says |a + ib| = 2, and squaring a modulus gives the sum of the squares of the parts.
